transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-10
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Casey Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (NovaHealth CTO), Ethan Brooks (NovaHealth ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Infra Lead), Ravi Desai (Product)
- Recording id: mf-20260310-nh-anchoring-01

Auto-summary: Quick sync on model anchoring (pin choices), fallback/safety-net rules, and next steps for a short shadow run. Discussed latency hotspots, quantization tradeoffs, and security constraints for VPC/KMS.

Topics:
1) Results review from last week's A/B shadow run
2) Model selection: anchor vs candidate pool and pinning strategy
3) Fallback tiers and emergency rollback mechanics
4) Security and private deployment gating
5) Action items and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight, 45 ish minutes. quick roll call — then arjun will walk through the latency heatmap and the pin matrix we discussed last week.
[00:16] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): hey lena, hey team, thanks. we had a pretty noisy week — infra changes plus some schema shifts so i'm hoping we can stabilise the pin set.
[00:29] Arjun (Redwood SE): cool. jumping in — i pushed the microbench last night, ran the model candidates on a Dedicated sim, quantized q4_0 and q8_0 variants, and collected p50/p95 token latencies under our traffic mix. the heatmap link is in the notes — tinyurl.com/nh-latency-03 — (uh) some of the bigger delta points are on long sequences for reprompt flows.
[01:02] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): yeah im seeing the same in our logs, the customer support flow with long context (40–60 turns) causes p95 spikes. sometimes kv cache warming is not consistent after our session expiry.
[01:18] Arjun (Redwood SE): exactly; warming + kv cache miss is the main cause. for the anchor model we recommend the smaller context-optimized variant — it holds well under quantization. larger models give better fidelity but cost and p95 go up.
[01:35] Ravi (Product): can you remind us of the exact tradeoff numbers? we need to justify to execs why we aren't using the biggest one.
[01:45] Arjun (Redwood SE): sure. rough numbers from sim — unquantized large: p50 token 12ms, p95 68ms, cost relative 1.0. q4_0: p50 9ms, p95 42ms, cost 0.45. q8_0: p50 8ms, p95 36ms, cost 0.6. accuracy diffs we measured on our eval suite: anchor loss +2.1% on prompt-level intent but human-eval delta ~1.3%, which your product team said was acceptable in the pilot.
[02:22] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): that sounds reasonable — lower cost is attractive. what's the safety-net if users hit bad regression in production?
[02:33] Lena (Redwood AE): good question. we typically suggest a soft-anchor approach: pin the anchor for 80% of traffic, shadow the higher-fidelity candidate for 20% and have an automated regression detector tied to your eval prompt set. if the detector trips two consecutive windows, auto-failover to a heavier model or a previous pinned version.
[02:54] Sofia (Infra Lead): how noisy is the detector? we can't have cascading rollbacks because of false positives.
[03:03] Arjun (Redwood SE): totally. the detector thresholds are tunable — we use combined metrics: token-level loss + semantic-sim change + latency SLO breaches. set conservatively for pilot. we can also add a human-in-the-loop confirmation during the first two incidents.
[03:25] Casey (Redwood CSM): we can include a slack webhook and a one-click rollback button in the console for the pilot. that tends to keep operations calm.
[03:35] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): would that require Dedicated or can we keep Hosted for now?
[03:41] Lena (Redwood AE): Hosted can do it, but if you want VPC peering and KMS control, that's Private. Dedicated sits in the middle — reserved GPU pools with better p95 guarantees. for the pilot i think many customers run Hosted with strict pinning and fallback rules.
[03:57] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): we need KMS and audit logs — SOC2 is in the works for us. so Private or Dedicated with KMS integration seems likely.
[04:08] Sophia (sic) Sofia (Infra Lead): yes, we need key rotation control and audit trails. can we lock model versions so that logs map to a stable hash?
[04:16] Arjun (Redwood SE): model versioning uses immutable hashes and the version id in logs — yes. audit logs include model hash, quantize profile, and node metadata for Private/Dedicated. Hosted includes the basics but not customer-managed KMS.
[04:32] Ravi (Product): any blockers for rolling a canary on Nov 18 as proposed?
[04:38] Lena (Redwood AE): timeline wise we can. next week arjun will deliver the finalized pinning matrix, and ethan runs shadow traffic for 48 hours, then we validate metrics. if that checks out we schedule canary traffic on 2026-03-20.
[04:55] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): that timeline sounds good. question — do you have any recommended escape-hatches besides rollback? e.g., degrade to cached responses, reduce generation length?
[05:06] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes — multiple escape hatches: 1) degrade to smaller anchor model, 2) fall back to last-known-good model version, 3) serve cached templated responses for high-frequency queries, 4) reduce max tokens and force shorter completions. we can chain them by priority.
[05:26] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): can we do a temporary routing to a lower-cost region to avoid outage? we worry about regional capacity.
[05:33] Arjun (Redwood SE): routing by region is supported — our smart router can failover to compatible model variant in another region. but cross-region latency and data residency are concerns. for NovaHealth, if you need data residency, that limits options.
[05:48] Sofia (Infra Lead): data residency is relevant for PHI-adjacent metadata. we need to map flows that touch PHI to Private with in-region keys.
[05:59] Lena (Redwood AE): noted — we'll flag PHI flows in the next pin matrix.
[06:05] Casey (Redwood CSM): back to the heatmap — arjun, any surprising outliers?
[06:10] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes — the reranker step in the pipeline causes bursts. when we run rerankers as separate calls, it multiplies latency. we suggested moving to batched rerank or local lightweight rerank to keep tail latency down.
[06:26] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): rerank is currently sync in our pipeline. switching to async would need product changes but likely doable.
[06:34] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): can we prioritize intent classification to avoid heavy rerank for simple queries?
[06:40] Arjun (Redwood SE): yep — tier queries by classifier confidence: high-confidence — no rerank; low-confidence — full pipeline. that reduces rerank volume significantly.
[06:51] Ravi (Product): curious — you mentioned q4_0 and q8_0 quant profiles. any concerns on hallucination with q4_0?
[06:59] Arjun (Redwood SE): small but measurable. q4_0 increases token-level noise for rare factual lookups. for your use case where hallucination is critical, we recommend shadowing q4_0 with a higher-fidelity candidate on a sample set for the first two weeks. if hallucination rate > threshold we hold on q4_0.
[07:18] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): what threshold do you recommend? our legal team wants under 0.2% factual error on discharge-summary prompts.
[07:26] Arjun (Redwood SE): for clinical-sensitive prompts i'd set 0.1% hard threshold for production; pilot target maybe 0.2% with more review. we'll include calibration tests.
[07:35] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): how do we instrument hallucination detectors?
[07:39] Arjun (Redwood SE): we have a candidate eval harness — pulls gold answers and runs semantic similarity + fact-check heuristics. we can integrate it into the eval pipeline and surface alerts to your dashboard.
[07:53] Lena (Redwood AE): small note — competitors we looked at for benchmarking were Anthropic (safety-forward), Vertex AI (tight cloud integrations) and Cohere (fast embeddings). for your workload the open models plus our quantization beats raw hosted endpoints on cost per token in our sim.
[08:11] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): that's helpful. security — what's the SOC2 story again?
[08:16] Lena (Redwood AE): Redwood has SOC2 Type II in our Hosted offering; for Private we provide the artifacts for your auditors and we integrate KMS/HSM as required. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[08:28] Sofia (Infra Lead): please include network diagrams and expected egress flows.
[08:32] Casey (Redwood CSM): will do, i'll include the network sketch and the peering checklist in the pack.
[08:40] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): okay, next — pin matrix. arjun?
[08:44] Arjun (Redwood SE): showing slide 3: the proposed anchor is model-v3-small-q8 (pinned), candidates: model-v3-medium (unquantized), model-v3-small-q4 (quantized aggressive). pin rules: anchor handles 80% traffic, medium candidate shadow 20%, q4 sample test 5% (subset). rollback policy: if eval delta > threshold or p95 breaches SLO for 3 consecutive windows, auto-pin previous stable version.
[09:14] Ravi (Product): three windows — what's window size?
[09:17] Arjun (Redwood SE): default is 15 minutes, but for pilot we recommend 30-minute windows to reduce noise.
[09:24] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): that seems long for patient-facing features — do we risk more user impact?
[09:29] Arjun (Redwood SE): tradeoff — longer windows reduce false positives, but faster detection shortens exposure. we suggested initial 30-minute windows with an ops guardrail (human-in-loop) for the first two triggers.
[09:42] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): i want visibility: could we log per-request model id + eval score to our aggregation?
[09:48] Arjun (Redwood SE): yes — logs include model id, hash, quant profile and an eval tag. we can push to your cloud logs or S3.
[09:58] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): any implications on cost for detailed logging?
[10:02] Lena (Redwood AE): standard access logs are included; high-resolution per-token logs are an add-on. we'll call that out.
[10:10] Sofia (Infra Lead): question on private deployment: if we deploy Private in our AWS account, how do we handle model updates? we need an immutable rollout path.
[10:18] Arjun (Redwood SE): updates are via versioned bundles you pull — we support canary bundles and staged deploys. you can pin by hash and roll forward only with approval. we also support air-gapped image installs for on-prem.
[10:33] Ravi (Product): important — who owns rollbacks operationally? our infra or Redwood?
[10:37] Lena (Redwood AE): by default customer-led; Redwood can operate in managed mode if you opt for our enterprise support. for pilot we suggest customer-led with Redwood advisory.
[10:48] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): fine. one more: are there any model license restrictions we need to watch?
[10:54] Arjun (Redwood SE): majority of candidates are permissive open weights but we'll flag any copyleft or extra-licensing models in the matrix.
[11:03] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): a quick nit — the reranker change: if we batch rerank, how does it affect QA ordering?
[11:10] Arjun (Redwood SE): batching preserves relative scores; you need to pick a batching window number that balances latency vs freshness. we'll send sample code for async rerank.
[11:21] Casey (Redwood CSM): follow-ups — lena will send the updated pin matrix doc and arjun will attach the heatmap + microbench.
[11:28] Lena (Redwood AE): yes, you'll get the matrix. also adding a short runbook with the escape hatches order.
[11:34] Ravi (Product): can you include a suggested throttling config so our app gracefully degrades during p95 spikes?
[11:40] Arjun (Redwood SE): will do — suggested leaky-bucket sizes and backoff.
[11:45] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): ok last item — timeline recap?
[11:49] Lena (Redwood AE): quick recap: arjun delivers final pin matrix and heatmap by 2026-03-12; ethan runs 48hr shadow 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-16; security team reviews Private/KMS by 2026-03-16; if all green we open canary on 2026-03-20.
[12:12] Maya (NovaHealth CTO): good. thanks everyone.
[12:15] Lena (Redwood AE): thanks all. we'll follow up in email with the artifacts — deck, matrix, heatmap. links: deck (tinyurl.com/nh-pilot-deck), heatmap (tinyurl.com/nh-latency-03), security pack (drive/restricted/nh-security-pack).
[12:36] Ethan (NovaHealth ML Eng): quick note — i'll flag three sample prompts I want considered high-risk and put them in the sheet right after this.
[12:44] Sofia (Infra Lead): i'll confirm VPC peering options and reply to the security doc thread.
[12:48] Lena (Redwood AE): great. action items and next steps captured in the meeting notes. end.
